Ba Sing Se and Us
Consider what Ba Sing Se expects of our realm this year.
Withhold Tribute from Ba Sing Se

Ba Sing Se is far away and its demands are many. Stop sending tribute. Where the crown is strong enough to expect it, each year of defiance costs the Earth King authority and angers them, but our standing grows.
Resume Tribute to Ba Sing Se
Make peace with the crown and send tribute again.

A courier in the green and gold of Ba Sing Se has arrived with a sealed command from [From.GetTitledFirstName]. Foreign armies have marched on the Earth Kingdom, and the crown reminds us that realms which owe it obedience are expected to stand with it.
We stand with Ba Sing Se.
This is not our war.
Ba Sing Se is a name we honour and little more. With the crown this weak, or this far away, our realm is answerable to no one but ourselves. We send nothing.
We recognise the Earth King as the head of the Earth Kingdom. Our realm sends a modest gift each year if we are a duke or greater (2, 4 or 8 gold), and otherwise governs itself.

The crown in Ba Sing Se is strong enough to expect tribute from us. Each year we send gold: 4 as a duke, 8 as a king and 16 as an emperor. Counts are spared unless the crown commands obedience. It goes into the treasury of Ba Sing Se, not to the Earth King personally. If our capital lies in the de jure kingdom of another independent Earth king, they collect it on the crown's behalf and gain prestige for it. We may withhold it, but the crown will remember.

Ba Sing Se commands obedience from realms this close to the capital. We pay full tribute (2 gold a year even as a count), and when foreign armies attack the Earth King we will be called to defend the crown. Refusing the call costs prestige and damages Ba Sing Se's authority.
So it is.

Defying Ba Sing Se

The Treasury of Ba Sing Se
Review the crown's treasury and the projects it is paying for.
Strengthen the Borders
Pay to garrison and fortify every province on the edge of our realm for ten years: larger garrisons, stronger forts and faster levy reinforcement.
Reform the Bureaucracy
Pay the clerks of the Grand Secretariat properly for ten years. Taxes are collected more efficiently, building is cheaper, and the treasury loses far less to graft.
Fund the Council of Five
Give the generals of the Council of Five the means to keep a standing force for ten years.
Fund the Dai Li
Give the Dai Li the means to watch the court and the city for ten years.
Send Relief to the Provinces

Send grain, builders and coin to the realms that owe Ba Sing Se. In Kyoshi's day such policies kept the peace between the states. Their rulers will think better of the crown, and the crown's authority grows.
Proclaim the Mandate of Ba Sing Se
Spend lavishly on ceremony, envoys and gifts to remind the states who wears the crown. Royal Authority increases greatly.
Draw on the Treasury
The treasury belongs to the crown, and we are the crown. Take 100 gold from it. Half of it reaches our purse, the rest disappears along the way, and word of it weakens the crown's authority.

The treasury is filled by the tribute of the states and belongs to the crown, not to us. Each year a tenth of it disappears into the pockets of clerks and officials, or only a little if the bureaucracy has been reformed. If a foreign power or a Chin pretender ever takes Ba Sing Se, they will help themselves to all of it.

Small projects last ten years. Great works change the whole Earth Kingdom for good, but the states remember every reach of the crown: resentment rises, and above 25 some states start refusing tribute. Relief to the provinces calms them. Resentment fades by 5 a year.
Very well.

Relief from Ba Sing Se
Great Work: The Royal Messenger Network

Post stations, relays of riders and messenger hawks along every road, day and night. Ba Sing Se's word reaches the far states in days instead of months, and the crown's reach grows with it. Costs 20 gold a year to keep running, and the states resent it.
Great Work: The Royal Roads

Paved roads and granaries across the Earth Kingdom. Every province of the Earth Kingdom outside the desert can feed larger armies and trades a little more, whoever owns it, and that includes invaders. Costs 15 gold a year to maintain.
Great Work: A Single Law for the Kingdom

Every state and town of the Earth Kingdom keeps its own laws. Replace them with one code written in Ba Sing Se. Tribute rises by half and the crown gains authority, but every state that pays it will hate the crown's laws for as long as they stand.
Great Work: Raise the Outer Wall
Raise a great outer wall around Ba Sing Se with conscripted labour from the provinces. The capital becomes nearly impregnable, but the conscription costs the crown authority and goodwill.

Riders in the green and gold of Ba Sing Se now pass through our lands every day, and every relay station has a royal clerk in it. The crown hears of everything we do within days, and expects more of us for it.
The crown's engineers have paved roads and raised granaries through our lands. Trade comes more easily. So, our generals note, would an army.
A herald from Ba Sing Se has read out a single code of law for the whole Earth Kingdom. The customs and courts our ancestors kept for generations are to give way to the clerks of the capital.
The crown has raised a great wall around Ba Sing Se, built by men taken from every province, ours included. Many did not come home.
Ba Sing Se's word is law.
We were here before the crown's clerks. We will pay no more.
Envoys from neighbouring states have come to us in secret. Ba Sing Se reaches too far, they say, and they have stopped sending tribute. They ask us to do the same.
They are right. We stop paying.
We keep faith with Ba Sing Se.
The treasury could no longer pay the riders and relay stations. The Royal Messenger Network has collapsed, and the far states are far again.
A great loss.
The treasury could no longer pay for repairs. The Royal Roads have fallen into disrepair.
